primary_claim: Among three methods for extracting domain-specific SAE features from a general web-trained SAE (GSAE) on Gemma 2B, finetuning the GSAE and training a Direct SAE best recover model loss on the domain data, while a Specialized SAE (SSAE) trained to reconstruct GSAE residuals finds features that are rarer in web text, newer relative to existing GSAE features, and rated higher quality by blind human labelers.

effect.metric: blind human-rated subject-specificity score (0-2 scale) averaged over 100 sampled features per SAE type
effect.value: SSAE features scored higher on average subject-specificity than Direct SAE features, for both college math and biology textbook domains

contradicts_or_qualifies: Notes concurrent work by Anthropic (September 2024 circuits update) addressing the same 'feature coverage' problem via a fourth method (mixing domain data into the pretraining dataset), which the author had not yet compared against
stated_future_work: Train SAEs on safety-relevant data (e.g. deception, persuasion, virology), including creating large datasets for such domains
For domains where sufficient web data is hard to find, turn to synthetic data
Show that a domain-specific SAE improves upon vanilla SAEs in some alignment task
Encourage others to train domain-specific SAEs and improve on the simple methods described
limitations_stated: The main limitation is scope: only a single model and a small number of datasets were investigated, so all claims are tentative
quote: the SSAE finds features that are rarer (on unstructured web text), newer (i.e. less similar to features that were already present in the GSAE), and higher-quality (as judged by human raters in a blind test).
